sections.text: INTRODUCTION TO THE HOPPER STUDY
Why have I been invited?

You have been invited to take part in this research study because seasonal respiratory viruses such as flu (influenza), Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV), and human metapneumovirus (hMPV) and many others commonly circulate during the winter season.

This study aims to improve understanding of respiratory viruses, including how they spread within households and how infections affect individuals. To do this, we are inviting households in advance so we can collect information both before any illness occurs and also begin sampling quickly if an infection develops.

We will ask you to provide a number of different samples and some basic information about you and your household including whether or not you are experiencing any symptoms. Regardless of whether you become unwell during this study, your participation will help improve understanding of seasonal respiratory viruses, how the human immune system responds to infection, and support public health responses during an outbreak.

Before you decide whether you want to participate, it is important that you understand why the research is being done and what the study will involve. Please take your time to read this information carefully and discuss it with others if you wish.
The full participant information sheet is available at: https://hopper.peoplewith.com/assets/HOPPER-PIS-Adult-CTPE-v.1.1.pdf or via the PeopleWith Research App.
Who is organising and funding the research?

The research is funded by the National Institute of Health and Care Research (NIHR) Health Protection Research Unit (HPRU) in Respiratory Infections, a partnership between Imperial College London and the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA). The study is being sponsored by Imperial College London.
Your GP will receive monetary support for the additional costs associated with informing you about the study.
Who has reviewed the study?

The study has been reviewed by the study sponsor (Imperial College London). It has been approved by an independent research ethics committee (REC) and has also been approved by the NHS Research Governance and Integrity Team.
Do I have to take part?
No. Taking part in this study is entirely voluntary.
If you decide to take part, you will be asked to sign a consent form. You can also access this information sheet online at any time from your study app, or from the study website homepage.

Even after you agree to take part, you are free to withdraw at any time without giving a reason via the study app or, by contacting the study team by email at hopper-study@imperial.ac.uk. Choosing not to take part, or choosing to withdraw later, will not affect the standard of care you receive now or in the future.
What is the purpose of the study?
The purpose of this study is to improve our understanding of how seasonal respiratory viruses spread within households and how they affect people living together.
Households are helpful for this research because infections can pass easily between people in close contact, allowing us to follow how illness develops over time.

Although much is already known about these viruses, like flu (influenza), RSV, and hMPV, they change over time. By collecting biological and environmental samples, along with some basic health information from you and your household, we aim to monitor currently circulating strains and update what is known about symptoms, how long people may be infectious, how easily infection spreads, and what factors affect the chance of becoming infected. The samples we collect will also allow us to better understand how the human immune system broadly responds to infection.
Before making any medical decisions, ALWAYS seek treatment advice or medical diagnosis directly from your Doctor or Health Care Professional.
Why have I been chosen?

You have been invited because we are approaching the winter season when seasonal respiratory viruses are most common. We are inviting people who live in households of three or more members so we can study how these infections spread and affect people in the community.
What will happen to me if I agree to take part?
This is an observational study, which means we will collect health-related information, samples and symptom information from you. We will not give you any treatment or alter your usual medical care.

You will not need to visit a clinic. The study will take place entirely at your home, and you will be asked to collect some samples yourself. Everything you need to collect samples will be sent directly to your home. A courier will collect your samples and return them to the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) or Imperial College London facilities.
More specific details of the enrolment process, and which samples to collect and when are given in the participant information sheet.
What do I have to do?
To take part in this study, you will need to follow the study procedures each day during the sampling period.

You should carefully read the study materials provided in your sampling pack, including the instruction booklet and online video guidance, and follow these alongside prompts from the study app. It is important to complete each step as instructed to ensure your participation in the study is successful.

You should continue to take any regular medications as prescribed and receive your usual medical care from your GP or healthcare team. If you have health concerns at any time, you should seek medical advice in the usual way. Nurses may check-in via text or call during the study to ensure you have the necessary support to enable you to engage with the study if you choose to take part.
If you are taking part in another research study, please inform the study team, as this may affect your eligibility.
What are the possible disadvantages and risks of taking part?
Taking part in this study involves minimal risk.

With your consent, we will access relevant information from your GP records using your NHS number. This information will be handled securely and pseudonymised (labelled with a code rather than your personal details), so the risk to your privacy is low. Further details are provided in the ‘Keeping Your Data Safe’ section.
If you agree to self-collecting samples for this research study, there is a risk of some pain or discomfort during the sample collection procedure.
What are the possible benefits of taking part?
There is no direct benefit to your health from taking part in the study.

The main benefit of taking part is indirect. The information collected in this study will help improve understanding of how respiratory infections spread, how they affect people, and how the body responds.
This knowledge will support better public health responses to seasonal respiratory virus outbreaks and help improve preparedness for future outbreaks.
Taking part may also help with the early detection of a respiratory infection, which could support timely monitoring and appropriate care if needed.

Right to object: The Company respects the right of an individual to object to data processing based on legitimate interest or the performance of a public interest task. The Company respects the right of an individual to object to direct marketing, including profiling.

DATA RETENTION, SECURITY AND STORAGE

The Company retains the data you the user input into the Application for the term and duration of use of the Application in order to ensure normal Application functionality. Upon termination of Application usage the Company will retain data for a period of two years unless specifically requested to erase the data under data protection laws.

On the event that you the user decide to delete your Account via the Application, systematic processes will permanently delete all data within forty eight hours. Deletion process cannot be reverse once implemented.
The Company utilise ISO27001 certified cloud computing platform Microsoft Azure as its cloud storage provide. Adequate organisational and technical safeguards are implemented to ensure data security.
Data is encrypted at all stages within the PeopleWith Platform, in-flight and at rest. Data encryption is implemented in the following ways:

Transparent Data Encryption: Data moving through PeopleWith’s Platform, from Azure Storage and Databases to the front end of the User Interface, is encrypted utilizing Azure’s Transparent Data Encryption protocols. When data arrives at is destination, it is unencrypted and presented accordingly.

Database Encryption: Data stored in a rest state in PeopleWith’s databases are encrypted with Database Encryption Keys implemented, dynamically rotated & updated on a period basis to ensure maximum defence against data breach.

In-Flight Encryption: Data is encrypted in-flight utilising Organisation Level Domain Verification Secure Socket Layer (SSL) for maximum verification and security to facilitate the processing of data through the internet.

We have put in place appropriate security measures to prevent your personal data from being accidentally lost, used or accessed in an unauthorised way, altered or disclosed. In addition, we limit access to your data to those designated employees and contractors who have a business need to know. They will only process your data on instruction, and they are subject to a duty of confidentiality.

We have put in place procedures to deal with any suspected personal data breach and will notify you and The Information Commissioner’s Office of a breach where we are legally required to do so. Additionally, if you have the right to complain to the Information Commissioner’s Office whose details can be found at: https://ico.org.uk.
